pr_title: Remove Blocking on GENERIC Pool in GET Snapshots
pr_body:
This aligns the way get snapshots works in `7.x` with how it works
in `master` exactly (except for masters ability to load snapshots across repos)
and thus fixes the deadlock in #69099.

No need to review the logic in detail here, it's the exact same logic as in master now so it probably rather makes sense comparing with master than looking at this in isolation.

Closes #69099
pr_comments: Jenkins run elasticsearch-ci/1  (snapshot test failure but unrelated and known to the features team)

issue_context.title: Deadlock in get-snapshots API
issue_context.body:
**Elasticsearch version** (`bin/elasticsearch --version`): 7.11.0

**Plugins installed**: Cloud

**JVM version** (`java -version`): Cloud

**OS version** (`uname -a` if on a Unix-like system): Cloud

**Description of the problem including expected versus actual behavior**:

A cluster was observed with all generic threads waiting here:

```
"elasticsearch[instance-0000000071][generic][T#1]" #33 daemon prio=5 os_prio=0 cpu=5894.11ms elapsed=559821.30s tid=0x00007f0af0746950 nid=0x1dc waiting on condition  [0x00007f0aef5f8000]
   java.lang.Thread.State: WAITING (parking)
	at jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe.park(java.base@15.0.1/Native Method)
	- parking to wait for  <0x00000006d6607c20> (a org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.BaseFuture$Sync)
	at java.util.concurrent.locks.LockSupport.park(java.base@15.0.1/LockSupport.java:211)
	at java.util.concurrent.locks.AbstractQueuedSynchronizer.acquire(java.base@15.0.1/AbstractQueuedSynchronizer.java:714)
	at java.util.concurrent.locks.AbstractQueuedSynchronizer.acquireSharedInterruptibly(java.base@15.0.1/AbstractQueuedSynchronizer.java:1046)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.BaseFuture$Sync.get(BaseFuture.java:248)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.BaseFuture.get(BaseFuture.java:76)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.FutureUtils.get(FutureUtils.java:45)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.support.AdapterActionFuture.actionGet(AdapterActionFuture.java:26)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.support.PlainActionFuture.get(PlainActionFuture.java:22)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.admin.cluster.snapshots.get.TransportGetSnapshotsAction.masterOperation(TransportGetSnapshotsAction.java:90)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.admin.cluster.snapshots.get.TransportGetSnapshotsAction.masterOperation(TransportGetSnapshotsAction.java:54)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.support.master.TransportMasterNodeAction.masterOperation(TransportMasterNodeAction.java:88)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.support.master.TransportMasterNodeAction$AsyncSingleAction.lambda$doStart$3(TransportMasterNodeAction.java:155)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.support.master.TransportMasterNodeAction$AsyncSingleAction$$Lambda$5714/0x0000000801b184c8.accept(Unknown Source)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.ActionRunnable$2.doRun(ActionRunnable.java:62)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.ThreadContext$ContextPreservingAbstractRunnable.doRun(ThreadContext.java:732)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.AbstractRunnable.run(AbstractRunnable.java:26)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(java.base@15.0.1/ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1130)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(java.base@15.0.1/ThreadPoolExecutor.java:630)
	at java.lang.Thread.run(java.base@15.0.1/Thread.java:832)
```

These threads are all waiting to retrieve the repository data, which itself needs generic threads, but there are no more generic threads available.

**Steps to reproduce**:

I have not tried, but I guess that you could reproduce this by hitting the get-snapshots API hard enough, especially if there are lots of old snapshots in the repository so retrieving the `RepositoryData` happens every time and is slow enough.

I suspect this was introduced in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/1cde4a6364ce26ab38c99d2bc08aa4a1d4ce3be6, so might affect all 7.x.y for x ≥ 6, but apparently not 8.z.
